scenes.line1: Can you always rerun your ML pipeline?
scenes.say: Can you rerun your machine learning pipeline and get the same results every single time? Let's see why that matters.

scenes.label: Repeatable
scenes.sub: Same code, data, and settings always give the same output.
scenes.say: Reproducibility means running the same code with the same data and settings always gives you the same output.
To make your pipeline reproducible, version your code, snapshot your data, lock your environment with tools like Docker, and set random seeds to control randomness.

scenes.title: Docker for reproducibility
scenes.say: Here's a real example. Build your environment with Docker, then run your pipeline and set a fixed random seed for training.

scenes.question: What if you skip data versioning?
scenes.wrong: It's fine if the code is versioned.
scenes.right: Without data versioning, results can change even if code and environment stay the same.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: skipping data versioning. Even if your code is tracked, your results can change if the data isn't versioned too.
